slot.subtopic: Interference – mirror images as coherent sources
slot.brief: Show a Lloyd's-mirror / two-source setup (or reflected ray acting as a virtual coherent source); ask the path difference and whether the central/reflecting-surface point is bright or dark.

stem: In the Lloyd’s-mirror setup shown, monochromatic light reflects with a phase change of $\pi$. At $O$, what is the geometric path difference, excluding this phase change, and the resulting interference?

verdicts.working: At O, the direct path SO and the reflected path (equivalent to S′O) are equal, so the geometric path difference is zero. The reflection adds a phase change of π, giving destructive interference.

working:
$SO=S'O=\sqrt{L^2+h^2}$
$\Delta_{\mathrm{geom}}=|SO-S'O|=0$
Reflection adds phase difference $\pi$.
$\therefore$ the waves interfere destructively at $O$; it is dark.

Independent check: At O, the direct path SO and the reflected path (equivalent to S′O) are equal, so the geometric path difference is zero. The reflection adds a phase change of π, giving destructive interference.
solution:
The reflected ray is equivalent to one from the image source $S'$, so $SO=S'O$.
$$\Delta_{\mathrm{geom}}=|SO-S'O|=0$$
Reflection adds a phase difference of $\pi$, so the waves interfere destructively at $O$; it is dark.

figure.description: Draw a horizontal mirror along the line y=0 from x=0 to x=L. Place a point source S at (0,h) above the mirror and a vertical screen at x=L. Mark point O on the screen at y=0, level with the mirror. Show the virtual image S' at (0,-h) below the mirror using a dashed outline. Draw the straight paths S–O and S'–O as thin lines; use a dashed style for the path from S' to O. Label the mirror, screen, S, S', O, h and L. Do not label any path difference or fringe type.

$\Delta_{\mathrm{geom}}=|SO-S'O|=0$

draft.distractor_notes: A: Ignores the phase reversal on reflection. C: Treats the reflection phase shift as geometric path difference. D: Treats the phase shift as a path difference and also incorrectly predicts constructive interference.
